summary.headline: DEE Development Engineers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to Rs 294.5 crore and EBITDA margin hit 16.9%, despite ~Rs 25 crore of dispatches slipping into Q2.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 294.5 crore, up 31.6% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 49.7 crore (16.9% margin vs 16% a year earlier). Management said about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches, deferred by export customers amid Middle East disruption, moved into Q2. Profit after tax was Rs 16.1 crore, and the Rs 300 crore preferential issue (net ~Rs 293 crore, ~Rs 225 crore earmarked for debt repayment) closed in July. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ revenue, EBITDA margin above 19%, and order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore.

segments.name: Piping and heavy fabrication (core)
segments.commentary: Management guides Rs 1,150-1,250 crore from piping for FY27, with the balance from subsidiaries including Thailand. Piping and heavy fabrication are the large majority of revenue and order book.

segments.name: Thailand subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about Rs 130 crore; target Rs 170-200 crore. Management says it is practically 100% booked for three years and no expansion is planned.

segments.name: Power PPA / non-core (Malwa, biomass pellets)
segments.commentary: Pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a., Muktsar) commissioned mid-Q1 FY27, so only partial contribution this quarter. Target combined non-core revenue around Rs 80 crore. Management said PPA EBIT went slightly negative (about Rs 1 crore) as fuel was diverted to the pellet plant; full operation expected from October.

segments.name: Seamless pipe plant (Anjar)
segments.commentary: Commissioned in FY26. Existing orders include about Rs 68 crore from L&T and a Rs 200 crore BHEL order, of which Rs 80-90 crore is expected to use in-house pipe. Management targets about 20% EBITDA on seamless pipe.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ reiterated; management called it a minimum and said the plan is to exceed it. Q1 is the weakest quarter, with Q4 typically the strongest.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided above 19%; management said it is 'absolutely on track'.
FY27 order inflow expected at least Rs 2,000 crore; Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the rest of the year.
Net debt expected to be no more than Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end; no plans for new debt this year.
Anjar plant utilisation expected at 60-65% this year and near 100% by end of FY28. Anjar revenue target of about Rs 1,500 crore by FY28-29.
Inventory days targeted at 150-160 by Q2 and 180-200 days for the overall working-capital cycle.
capex_capacity: Anjar pipe fabrication facility fully operational; seamless pipe plant commissioned in FY26. Plan is roughly 50-50 split between captive and outright-sale use of Anjar capacity.
Biomass pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a.) at Malwa Power Plant, Muktsar, commissioned in Q1 FY27.
Nuclear sector entry planned via a partner; management aims to finalise the partnership agreement in Q2 FY27.
No capex or capacity expansion planned at Thailand facility.
Preferential issue proceeds of about Rs 293 crore net: about Rs 224-225 crore for debt or working-capital repayment, balance for general corporate purposes.
demand_pricing: Revenue slippage: about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches deferred to Q2 as export customers delayed take-offs due to the Middle East situation; material is ready.
GE: GT orders continuing; HRSG order from GE yet to come, though an agreement exists for around 15-16 units. A GE meeting is set for 14 September.
Siemens: MoU for GT piping starting at 10 units next year, then 15, then 25-30 units. Each GT unit is about EUR 1-1.5 million. Siemens team to visit Anjar in the third week of August.
BHEL: slower than expected, but about Rs 200 crore order received last quarter and more tenders expected to be finalised next quarter. L&T has awarded all orders offloaded so far.
Export mix: about 50% export and 50% domestic for FY27. The order book includes about Rs 400 crore of India HRSG work and about Rs 200 crore from Thailand.
Gross margin pressure attributed to higher material content in power-sector jobs (versus job-work) and the mix shift. Management said conversion costs are lower for power jobs.
Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited domestic order of Rs 386.82 crore received in the quarter, described as one of the largest single orders in recent history.
Gulf reconstruction: inquiries are coming via OEMs; not yet direct, and not included in projections for five years.

qa_highlights.question: Status of GE HRSG orders and Siemens GT piping?
qa_highlights.answer: GE GT orders continue, HRSG order yet to come despite agreement for 15-16 units. Siemens MoU for 10 units next year, 15 the year after, then 25-30. Each GT unit about EUR 1-1.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 2,000 crore order inflow guidance still valid given delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said inflow may exceed Rs 2,000 crore. Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the remainder of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PPA EBIT turn negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Limited fuel meant the company prioritised the pellet plant over the power plant. Full operation of both is expected from October when new fuel arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt trajectory and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt Rs 718 crore at Q1 close versus Rs 733 crore at FY26 close, expected to fall to Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end. Rs 224 crore used for working-capital limits reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher material content in power-sector jobs and a mix shift away from job-work. Management still expects EBITDA above 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone rate 25.17%; consolidated effective rate about 20-21% because of the Thailand subsidiary and subsidy income.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 718 crore at Q1 FY27 close
financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 733 crore at FY26 close

risks_watch: Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches deferred to Q2 by export customers amid the Middle East situation; watch whether they are actually delivered in Q2.
GE HRSG order (agreement for ~15-16 units) not yet placed; management says it will not affect FY27 top line, with a GE meeting set for 14 September.
Gross margin pressure from higher material content in power-sector jobs and mix shift away from job work; EBITDA >19% guidance depends on this offsetting.
Working capital: creditor days fell to 34 from 66 and debtor days rose to 123 from 99; the target of 180-200 day cycle and inventory days of 150-160 by Q2 need to be tracked.
Pellet plant and PPA division: PPA EBIT turned slightly negative (~Rs 1 crore) on fuel constraints; full operation expected from October when new fuel arrives. BHEL orders are slower than expected.
key_quotes: Around Rs. 25 crores of dispatches scheduled for Q1 got pushed into Q2 primarily on the oil and gas side, where a few of our export customers deferred take-offs given the situation in the Middle East.
As far as your question on EBIT is concerned, frankly, we had commissioned our pellet plant a bit earlier.
we remain fully committed, fully committed for our top line of Rs. 1.500 crores plus and EBIDTA margin of more than 19%.
Our plan is that by the end of next year, we should be utilizing almost 100% of the available capacity at Anjar.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on FY27 guidance (Rs 1,500 crore+ revenue, EBITDA above 19%, order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore) and said it was "absolutely on track", but was less definite on timing, with GE HRSG orders, BHEL tenders and the PPA fuel supply all described as slower than expected. Answers on working capital, tax rate and gross margin were given with specific figures, though some answers were hedged as "guesswork" (e.g., EPC contracting models of Adani/L&T).

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue of Rs 1,500 crore+ (a minimum), EBITDA margin above 19%, and order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore against a Rs 2,428 crore order book, but Q1 revenue slipped about Rs 25 crore into Q2, no new capex is planned beyond commissioned assets, and Anjar utilisation is only 60-65% this year.
